Recently, there have been signs that domestic demand for copper has picked up in China. This has led to an opening of the SHFE/LME arbitrage and a rally in spot premium quotations. In the last two weeks, traders reported that quotations for imported cathode were in the range of $80-100/t whilst those for SXEW between $70-90/t. As a result, more imported cathode has been released in the market since the end of May. Currently, we estimate that inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses amount to 360,000380,000t of copper cathode. This represents a decline of approximately 30,000t from late May, which is a slower rate of decline than was reported in April. CRU heard reports from market participants that a range © 2011 CRU International Limited **confidential** **June 2011** www.crumonitor.com of 200,000-300,000t is considered a normal level for cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses. We believe the top end of this range represents the current situation in the market, and therefore there is limited scope for further significant inventory declines. According to customs data, China imported 254,738t of unwrought copper and copper semis in May, down by 3% m-o-m. Industry participants had different expectations as they anticipated that cathode imports should increase due to the favorable SHFE/LME price ratio improvement. However, most traders expect that cathode imports will recover in June, supported by the enthusiasm the positive SHFE/LME arbitrage fuels. # **Power shortages impact copper smelters** Market participants are concerned about the impact of power shortages on the Chinese copper industry. Usually, copper semis production is more affected by power rationing compared to copper smelting operations. This is because Zhejiang, Jiangsu and Guangdong, which happen to be major copper semis production hubs, tend to encounter severer power shortage issues compared to other provinces. However, CRU heard that this year copper smelters operations are being impacted by power shortages as well. The Tongling Nonferrous Jinlong plant, with 350,000t/y smelting and 400,000t/y refining capacity, reported that its refined copper production was affected by power shortages in Anhui province in late May and early June. Unlike semis fabricators who can shift operations from electricity peak hours to less power intensive hours in a day, copp

er smelters are affected when they face power shortages. We estimate that refined copper output at the Jinlong plant contracted by about 4,000t. In addition, operations at the Tongling Nonferrous Jinchang plant, with 180,000t/y smelting and 180,000t/y refining capacity, were also affected, with refined copper output down by about 1,000t as a result. With the electricity consumption peak season now approaching, we project that power shortages at the Jinlong and Jinchang plants may last until August. Some market insiders attribute the decline in domestic refined copper output primarily to the impact of power shortages on copper smelters. Our view is that even though this is one of the reasons it is not the principal one. According to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), China produced 439,000t of refined copper in May, down by 3.3% m-o-m. We believe that it was mainly the fall in secondary copper output caused by scrap shortages that led to a contraction in refined copper production. Moreover, falling copper prices in May also impacted the enthusiasm of some refined copper producers for increasing their output. # **Weak demand season approaches** NBS data showed that China produced 970,000t of copper semis in May, an increase of 20% y-o-y and 7% m-o-m. We do believe that Chinese copper consumption improved in May. Furthermore, the fall in copper prices last month triggered restocking among some semis fabricators. As already mentioned, cathode inventories in SHFE and Shanghai bonded warehouses declined whilst semis output rose. In addition, some semis fabricators said they intend to run at full capacity before the expected power shortages take place in July and August. With the seasonal weakness in Q3, copper tube and flat rolled product makers reported that utilisation rates started to decline in June, however, to a limited extent. The majority anticipate that new orders will decline in July. On the other hand, copper wirerod producers reported that their operating rates remained at high levels, and have positive expectations for new orders. © 2011 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **June 2011** www.crumonitor.com To conclude, we anticipate that domestic refined copper consumption will decline gradually in July and August. LME 3-month copper prices hovered within a $8,900-9,200/t range in the past two weeks, as sentiment about the financial environment alternated between optimism and pessimism. Sim

ilarly, SHFE 3-month copper prices fluctuated between RMB67,150-68,610/t. China’s consumer price index in May reached 5.5%, which was the highest level since July 2008. As a result, controlling inflation remains a major task for the Chinese government. In response, China’s central bank raised the deposit reserve ratio by 0.5% to 21.5%, effective from 20<sup>th</sup> June. Therefore, we anticipate that domestic copper consumption faces downside pressure due to the continued tightened credit policy which will affect buying activity. In addition, weak seasonal demand and power shortages may both affect refined copper consumption in July and August. We noticed that SHFE cathode inventories increased slightly to 87,310t this week, up by 1,147t compared to two weeks ago.  However, some positive news for the copper market is that social housing construction may accelerate in Q3. In the first five months of the year, 3.4 million units of affordable housing started construction. According to plans, 10 million units of affordable housing are expected to commence in 2011. It is therefore anticipated that more affordable houses will begin construction in the remainder of 2011. We believe that SHFE 3-month copper prices will fluctuate around RMB68,000/t in the next two weeks, partially driven by the outcome of the Federal Reserve’s interest rate setting meeting taking place on 21<sup>st</sup> and 22<sup>nd</sup> June.
